name: Question 3
problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14096050/assets/e11ec3379c969bbc8499f36978f3a39efe1342ee6563569949dbcb61611ab5f4.png)

A cube of ice is melting uniformly at a rate of $6\,{\text{cm}}^{3}\text{/min},$ where $x$ is the length of its edge. How fast is each edge of the ice block decreasing when the volume of the cube is $8\,{\text{cm}}^{3}?$
worked_solution:
Let $V$ be the volume of the ice cube. We are given that 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}V}{\text{d}t}=-6\,{\text{cm}}^{3}/\text{min}.\end{aligned}
$$

We would like to find $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}$ when $V=8\,{\text{cm}}^{3}.$

We start with the formula for the volume of the cube:

$$
V={x}^{3}
$$

Now, we differentiate with respect to time using the chain rule, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(V) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({x}^{3}) \\ \frac{\text{d}V}{\text{d}t} & =3{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}.\end{aligned}
$$

Before we plug in the known values, we need to find the value of $x$ when $V=8\,{\text{cm}}^{3}.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}V & ={x}^{3} \\ 8 & ={x}^{3} \\ x & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

We can now plug $x=2$ and $\frac{\text{d}V}{\text{d}t}=-6$ into the expression for $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}V}{\text{d}t} & =3{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} \\ -6 & =3(2)^{2}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} \\ \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =-\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the sides of the cube are decreasing at a rate of $\frac{1}{2}\,\text{cm}/\text{min}$ at the moment when $x=2\,\text{cm}.$

Question 3
?

A cube of ice is melting uniformly at a rate of 6cm3/min, where x is the length of its edge. How fast is each edge of the ice block decreasing when the volume of the cube is 8cm3?

a
 32cm/min
b
 12cm/min
c
 23cm/min
d
 1cm/min
e
 2cm/min
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Let V be the volume of the ice cube. We are given that dVdt=−6cm3/min.

We would like to find dxdt when V=8cm3.

We start with the formula for the volume of the cube: V=x3

Now, we differentiate with respect to time using the chain rule, and we get

ddt(V)=ddt(x3)dVdt=3x2⋅dxdt.

Before we plug in the known values, we need to find the value of x when V=8cm3. We get

V=x38=x3x=2.

We can now plug x=2 and dVdt=−6 into the expression for dxdt. This gives

dVdt=3x2⋅dxdt−6=3(2)2⋅dxdtdxdt=−12.

Therefore, the sides of the cube are decreasing at a rate of 12cm/min at the moment when x=2cm.
